ledger.claim: The driver's own trace shows he held position inside the pickup geofence for only 229 continuous seconds, from 18:54:34 to 18:58:23, before cancelling at 18:58:27. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 300 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), and the STANDARD zone minimum dwell is also 300 seconds. The shortfall is 71 seconds. Under POL-NS-06 the cancellation fee is not chargeable and must be refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages.

The driver's arrival marker is not false and the clock is not recomputed: the trace places him at the pickup pin (min_distance_m 0.0) at the arrival timestamp, and his speed at that moment is 0.0 kph, well under the 15 kph motion threshold of POL-NS-05. So the 229-second dwell is the effective dwell, measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, and it falls 71 seconds short of the 300-second minimum. The shortfall is real, not an artifact of a false marker.

The rider was at the pickup and actively coordinating. At 18:55:34, during the waiting window, the rider sent 'im at the lobby, coming out' - a locating message naming their own position. The driver's only reply, 'ok', came at 18:55:49, 15 seconds later, and the driver then cancelled at 18:58:27 without ever moving to the lobby. The rider's device track places them within 12.5 m of the pin for the whole window, well inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, across 48 qualifying fixes. Under POL-NS-04 the rider is exonerated and the fee refunded in full with no driver compensation.

The driver's own statement confirms he abandoned the pickup: 'Rider was not visible and I had another booking waiting.' That is not a rider no-show; it is the driver choosing a different job over the fare he had accepted. The rider had told him in chat they were at the lobby and coming out, and the driver read that message at 18:55:54. The cancellation at 18:58:27 came 2 minutes 33 seconds after that read receipt, with the rider still inside the geofence.

The fare ledger confirms the rider was charged SGD 4.00 and that nothing has been refunded: payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00. The amount contested is exactly the cancellation-fee line, so the refund is the full SGD 4.00. No booking or platform fee was charged on this cancelled trip, so there is nothing else to refund.

ledger.claim: The driver's profile does not rescue the fee. His no_show_terminations_30d is 0 and his completed_trips_30d is 132, so the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip and there is no basis to withhold compensation on that ground - but equally there is no verified no-show here for POL-NS-07 to compensate, because POL-NS-01 limb (c) fails on the 71-second dwell shortfall. The fee is refunded and no driver compensation is payable.

The rider's profile shows no pattern of abuse: no_show_disputes_30d is 0, disputes_with_counterparty_90d is 0, and deviation_claims_60d is 0. There is no basis under POL-NS-09(c) or (d) to escalate this case, and the rider's clean record is consistent with a rider who was genuinely at the lobby when the driver cancelled.

The driver's own GPS trace places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius for a continuous qualifying run of 229 seconds, from 18:54:34 to 18:58:23, with 24 qualifying fixes — so POL-NS-02's arrival test is satisfied and the dispute turns on dwell duration under POL-NS-01(c).

The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 18:54:34 and a wait_timer_started event at 18:54:36, and the driver terminated the trip at 18:58:27 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW with no boarding event — POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) are therefore met on the record.

The free waiting period in force for this trip is 300 seconds, read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, and the driver's in-geofence dwell of 229 seconds falls 71 seconds short of it — so on the face of the arithmetic POL-NS-06 requires the cancellation fee to be refunded in full and no driver compensation is payable. I concede this point: the record does not support the fee on the dwell limb.

The only route that could rescue the fee is POL-NS-06 limb (i), which permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed where a traffic_advisory covering the pickup road was in force — but EV-ADVIS-02708-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so limb (i) is unavailable and the shortfall cannot be cured. I do not assert the advisory against a MISSING artifact.

The rider's own track is present and stationary: 48 fixes, all at 0.0 kph, with a maximum distance of 12.47 m from the pickup pin, well inside the 100 m STANDARD rider_presence_radius_m — so the rider was at the pin throughout the waiting window and POL-NS-04 limb (c) is satisfied on admissible fixes.

The rider sent a locating message at 18:55:34 ('im at the lobby, coming out') and the driver replied 'ok' at 18:55:49, within 120 seconds — so POL-NS-04 limb (b) fails and the rider-contact clause does not exonerate the rider; the dispute is decided under POL-NS-01 and POL-NS-06.

The arrival marker is not false: the driver's qualifying in-geofence run begins at the 'arrived' timestamp itself (dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0), so POL-NS-05 does not displace the clock and no false-arrival referral arises.

The fare ledger shows the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee charged to the rider with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and the line reconciles with the platform_policy figure of SGD 4.00 — so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect, and the amount to be refunded is the cancellation-fee line only.

The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 0, below the 4-or-more limb, and 0 divided by completed_trips_30d of 132 is 0.00, below the 0.08 rate limb — so no escalation under POL-NS-09(d) arises from the driver's side.

The rider's profile shows no_show_disputes_30d of 0 and disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0, and the driver's shows disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0, so neither POL-NS-09(c) nor POL-NS-09(d) is engaged on the profile counters.

The GPS trace is clean for policy purposes: 100.0% coverage, 80 fixes at a 10 s cadence, no gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0, and the chat log's 2 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count — so no POL-NS-08 limb (a) to (d) impairment applies and the dwell arithmetic stands undiscounted.

ruling.explanation:
Ruling: the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full, with no driver compensation.

THIS DECIDES THE CASE. Both parties agree on the arithmetic and the evidence confirms it. The driver's GPS trace (EV-GPS-02708) places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from 18:54:34 to 18:58:23 - one continuous qualifying dwell of 229 seconds on 24 qualifying fixes. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 300 seconds, read from trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec (EV-TRIP-02708). The driver cancelled at 18:58:27, 71 seconds short. Under POL-NS-01 limb (c) and POL-NS-06 the fee is not chargeable, and because it was charged (EV-FARE-02708: cancellation_fee SGD 4.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), the whole SGD 4.00 is returned. This refund comes from POL-NS-06, not POL-NS-01.

The only route that could have cured the shortfall - POL-NS-06 limb (i), summing separate in-geofence intervals - requires a present, populated traffic advisory, and EV-ADVIS-02708-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT). Limb (i) is unavailable, so the 229-second single run is the whole dwell. The driver's claim stating this (with the impairment disclosed) is accepted; the rider's equivalent claim is addressed in the audit below.

Arrival itself is established (POL-NS-02). The qualifying run begins at the arrival timestamp itself (dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0, 0.0 kph at the marker), so POL-NS-05 finds no false marker, the waiting clock is not recomputed, and no false-arrival referral arises. A genuine marker does not help the fee here: it fixes when the clock starts, not whether the wait was served out.

The rider's alternative route, POL-NS-04 (rider contact unanswered by driver), does not apply. Limb (b) requires that the driver neither replied within 120 seconds nor placed a call, and EV-CHAT-02708 shows the rider's 18:55:34 message ('im at the lobby, coming out') answered by the driver's 'ok' at 18:55:49 - 15 seconds later. Limbs (a) and (c) are met (the rider's device track sits within 12.5 m of the pin across 48 fixes, well inside the 100 m STANDARD radius), but limb (b) fails, so POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider. It changes nothing: the fee is refunded under POL-NS-06 in any event, whether or not the rider was present.

The driver's statement ('Rider was not visible and I had another booking waiting') is recorded. It carries no weight_multiplier, so it enters neither the minimum nor the maximum of the confidence cap, and it does not alter the arithmetic. The rider's argument that this shows the driver chose another job over the accepted fare is noted and is not needed to reach the refund.

Profiles decide nothing here. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip (driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d 0; 0/132 = 0.00), and neither POL-NS-09(c) nor POL-NS-09(d) is engaged (rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d 0; disputes_with_counterparty_90d 0 on both sides). Reader's note: driver_profile.prior_no_show_flags (2) is a lifetime counter and is not the trailing-30-day field any clause reads.

Evidence integrity: the GPS trace is clean (100.0% coverage, 80 fixes at a 10 s cadence, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0); the chat log's 2 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count; the fare line reconciles to the SGD 4.00 in platform_policy. No POL-NS-08(a)-(d) impairment applies, so the dwell arithmetic stands undiscounted and the confidence cap is the weight of the artifacts carrying the deciding fact - EV-GPS-02708 (229 s dwell) and EV-TRIP-02708 (300 s free wait), both at 1.0 - so confidence is not capped below that figure.

The monetary effect (SGD 4.00) is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, so it executes automatically on issue; either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
